caption: ‘25. Probably the hardest year of my life. I found myself in the darkest place I’ve ever been to the point where I was looking in the mirror and  I couldn’t recognize myself and it was the scariest thing I’ve ever been through. I watched people turn their back on me, not knowing that I was struggling mentally. I couldn’t be the Jada that everybody knew and that ate me alive because I’ve always been “too hard” to ask for help. I fought like hell and stood on my testimony every step of the way, and God showed me that my purpose was greater than anything I could ever do on the court.. he never let me give up and he never let me stop smiling. He’s equipped me with the tools that I need to battle anything that gets thrown at me. I truly am blessed and extremely grateful for where I am today. I’m so thankful for those who never gave up on me, never let my flame die out, and those who brought the old Jada back. 2025 wasn’t just the year that I hit rock bottom, it was also the year that I overcame the most adversity that I’ve faced up until this point. To say the least I’m excited for 2026, I’m in a place that little Jada always dreamed of and surrounded by people that God purposely placed me around. #ochoyear🥷🎱

caption:
WOW — it’s officially been a whole year since the start of my back injury. I had no idea, not even a clue, that the next twelve months would become some of the hardest of my entire life — physically, mentally, and emotionally. There were days where I truly felt like I had hit rock bottom. Days where the pain, the uncertainty, and the constant setbacks made me question everything. It felt like one thing after another kept piling on, and with no clear answers, I honestly thought I was going crazy 🤪. I’ve cried more tears than I ever thought I could. I’ve sat through more appointments, X-rays, MRIs, injections, medications, and breakdowns than I can count… all eventually leading to surgery. And yes — after all of that, I still can’t feel my foot 😂.

But today, a year later, I can say with a full heart that I’m grateful it happened. This year broke me down, but it also rebuilt me. It reshaped the woman I am becoming. It changed the teammate I strive to be and the friend I choose to show up as. It pushed me closer to my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ when I needed Him most. It showed me the importance of having a small, trusted circle — the people who stay when everything else feels like it’s falling apart. And honestly, I think I lived more hours in the athletic training room and PT clinic than anywhere else… but even those moments became part of my story.

I’m not fully back yet, and there are still unknowns, but I’m overwhelmed with gratitude for the people who carried me when I couldn’t carry myself.

Huge shoutout to my mom and dad, my brother, and my amazing grandmother who prayed over me endlessly. To all the family and friends thank you for your support near and far. To my best friends who loved me at my lowest and never made me feel alone. To my teammates who supported me through every high and every setback. And to my coaches, athletic trainers at Iowa State, my physical therapists, Dawson and Doney, and my surgeon — thank you for believing in me when I struggled to believe in myself. Here’s to healing. Here’s to resilience. Here’s to the girl who refused to quit, even when quitting felt easier. I’m so ready to play healthy again! 🤍🙏🏼

ATHLETE SPOTLIGHT 🔦

I have the privilege of working with Jack, a top-tier tight end at Iowa State on several lingering issues that just wouldn’t go away after a few injuries.

Jack is a high-level athlete in a high-level program. While the team staff does an incredible job (seriously, they’re the best of the best), sometimes it takes a fresh perspective to address those chronic, nagging problems.

That’s exactly what my approach is built around: a deep, full-body assessment to uncover the root cause of dysfunction, not just symptom management.

Through our work, we were able to achieve:
✅ Significant pain reduction
✅ Drastically improved movement and function
✅ A return to school feeling better than he has in a long time

This is why private, individualized care matters. No rushed visits. No insurance limitations. Just focused, performance-driven rehab built around the athlete.

Jack’s getting back after a rough rehab year and I’m excited to be part of the journey. Let’s keep pushing toward those big goals.

caption: First of all, I want to thank god for blessing me these past four years for letting me play the game i love with the best teammates i could ask for. I’ve played with a special group of guys through the years and It was a heck of a ride & I’ve enjoyed every second of it. I am so happy to be part of a program that will be talked about forever. Especially making it to state, back to back to back to back ! It has never been done in history & we were the first ones to do it. To the coaches, there is nothing more you could’ve done, that you haven’t did. You guys stayed pushing us, making sure we were studying film every single day, & most importantly making sure we are doing right in the classroom. To the fans y’all fill my heart with joy. i can’t remember a time we were down by points & y’all giving up on us. You stay cheering us on when we were trying to make a comeback, loud every single game and I just thank yall for that. & Now it’s time to move on to the next chapter in my life. Franklin i will never forget the memories we have put up in the past. This is coming from the bottom of my heart, Thank you ❤️

caption:
Rosemount Softball, where do I even begin! Thank you for the countless life lessons, advice, encouragement, heartache and support all these years! It’s way more then the wins in loses! Its the relationship I have built these past 12+ years that will last a life time! To all the coaches that I have had over the many years! Thank you for pushing me to be the best athlete, person and leader! For encouraging me to chase after my dreams at a very young age! I would not be were I am today with out your mentorship! This past high school season has been an absolute dream come true! To have a perfect season your senior year and to Win the State Tournament! I could not have asked for a better way to end my high school career! I still can’t believe that I will never wear a Rosemount Irish Uniform ever again!

To all the little girls in the program! Don’t stop believing in yourself, go after your dreams, work hard, be the best teammate you can be and most importantly HAVE FUN! It’s probably hard for you to think about it, but there will be a day where you will have to put the Rosemount Jersey on for the last time to compete with your best friends! Don’t take anything for granted it goes by fast! Cherish all the hard practices, long hot tournaments and the long car rides from tournaments! 

They always say it’s hard to say goodbye to something that means so much to you! Thank you Rosemount Softball for all the memories all theses years! 2x State Champion has a good ring to it! #5out 🤍☘️🥎
